about: The Agimus tibi gratias is a short thanksgiving traditionally said after a meal. Those gathered thank almighty God for all his benefits and confess that he lives and reigns for ever.

seg.tr: We give you thanks, almighty God,

fn.w001: With “grátias”, it forms the fixed expression “grátias ágere” — to give thanks. Its ending expresses the first-person plural.
fn.w002: The dative identifies God as the personal recipient of thanksgiving.
fn.w003: The accusative plural is the object of “Ágimus” in the idiom meaning to give thanks.
fn.w004: The vocative adjective agrees with “Deus” and names the addressee's almighty power.
fn.w005: Here “Deus” is vocative: it identifies the addressee already indicated by “tibi”.

fn.w006: The preposition with the ablative introduces the benefits for which thanks are given.
fn.w007: The adjective includes the complete range of benefits, not only the gift of the meal.
fn.w008: The ablative governed by “pro” names God's benefits as the reason for thanksgiving.
fn.w009: The possessive relates the benefits to the God whom the faithful address.

seg.tr: who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

fn.w010: The relative is a nominative subject and resumes the God named by “Deus”. Its second-person verbs continue the direct address to God.
fn.w011: The present second person predicates life of the God who remains directly addressed.
fn.w012: The conjunction coordinates two predicates of the same addressee.
fn.w013: The present second person confesses God's continuing reign.
fn.w014: The preposition with the accusative introduces the fixed formula of unbounded duration.
fn.w015: The accusative plural is governed by “in”.
fn.w016: The genitive plural completes the idiom “ages of ages”, expressing eternity.
fn.w017: The final assent embraces the whole thanksgiving and confession.
